Q: Any way to auto-update/push git submodule (without a cmd to do so) A:

I wrote and Azure DevOps extension to help update git submodules.

https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=CodeMonkeyProjectiles.git-submodule-updater

Add this task to the top of the pipeline. Then when your pipeline runs from a pull request, the task will add comments to the PR if the submodules are out of date. It can also start an new PRs to update each submodule.

Q: Azure Devops pipelines - submodules not get updated by default A:

Q: Populate Field Description, Status Bar Text, Control Tip Text in MS Access from a table A:

First-off: exactly what version of MS Access are you using? (Access 2016? 2013? 2007? 2003?) and what kind of database files are you using (.mdb, .accdb, any Linked Servers?).

Please share the CREATE TABLE definition of your Data Dictionary table and some excerpted rows - so we can properly understand the situation. Are you using a single table (which, presumably, contains details for columns - but not for other types of objects, like tables and views/queries?).

Speaking of Data-Dictionaries, are you familiar with MSysObjects and other Access built-ins?

Also, when you say "status bar" - are you referring to Access' main UI's status-bar? - or the status-bar in your own Access Forms that live inside your database? Or something else?

Q: How can I get the current time in milliseconds in PHP? A:

This works even if you are on 32-bit PHP:

[$msec, $sec] = explode(' ', microtime());

$time_milli = $sec.substr($msec, 2, 3); // '1491536422147'
$time_micro = $sec.substr($msec, 2, 6); // '1491536422147300'

Note this doesn't give you integers, but strings. However this works fine in many cases, for example when building URLs for REST requests.


If you need integers, 64-bit PHP is mandatory.

Then you can reuse the above code and cast to (int):

[$msec, $sec] = explode(' ', microtime());

// these parentheses are mandatory otherwise the precedence is wrong!
//                  ↓                        ↓
$time_milli = (int) ($sec.substr($msec, 2, 3)); // 1491536422147
$time_micro = (int) ($sec.substr($msec, 2, 6)); // 1491536422147300

Or you can use the good ol' one-liners:

$time_milli = (int) round(microtime(true) * 1000);    // 1491536422147
$time_micro = (int) round(microtime(true) * 1000000); // 1491536422147300
